assumptions.condition: The contexts are independent across rounds with common law \(P_X\), and \(P_X\) has a density \(p_X\) on \(\mathcal X\) satisfying \(c_X\le p_X(x)\le C_X\) almost everywhere.

The observed reward obeys \(Y_t=\mu_{A_t}(X_t)+\sigma\varepsilon_t\), where \(\varepsilon_t\mid(H_{t-1},X_t,A_t)\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\) and the variables \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_T\) are conditionally independent innovations given the realized contexts, assignments, and past observed histories.

standard.name: conditionally independent Gaussian innovation model under adaptive sampling

assumptions.condition: For each \(a\in\mathcal A\), the regression satisfies \(|\mu_a(x)-\mu_a(x')|\le L\|x-x'\|_2^\beta\) for all \(x,x'\in\mathcal X\).
For every \(u\) satisfying \(0\le u\le\delta_0\), \(P_X\{0<|\tau_P(X)|\le u\}\le C_0u^\alpha\).

standard.name: local Tsybakov margin condition for covariate bandits

assumptions.condition: The benchmark \(\pi_0\) is fixed before the experiment and is identical for every \(P\) in the model class.

standard.name: fixed-gap compatibility with the bounded contrast envelope

assumptions.condition: The mean and local-margin constants satisfy \(C_0(2M)^\alpha\ge1\).

standard.name: fixed-gap compatibility with the Tsybakov margin envelope

assumptions.condition: The fixed benchmark assigns inferior treatment with population mass at least \(b_0\): \(\mathbb E_{P_X}[(1-\pi_0(X))\mathbf 1\{\tau_P(X)>0\}+\pi_0(X)\mathbf 1\{\tau_P(X)<0\}]\ge b_0\).

novel.justification: The condition isolates benchmarks whose gain genuinely depends on the inferior-arm regression. It holds with \(b_0=1/2\) for balanced randomization and with a positive constant for any pre-specified policy bounded away from zero and one.

definitions.name: Hölder-margin Gaussian law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}=\{P: X_t\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P_X,\ c_X\le p_X\le C_X,\ Y_t=\mu_{A_t}(X_t)+\sigma\varepsilon_t,\ \varepsilon_t\mid(H_{t-1},X_t,A_t)\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\text{ are conditionally independent innovations},\ \|\mu_a\|_\infty\le M,\ |\mu_a(x)-\mu_a(x')|\le L\|x-x'\|_2^\beta\ \text{for each }a,\ P_X(0<|\tau_P(X)|\le u)\le C_0u^\alpha\ \text{for }0\le u\le\delta_0,\ \alpha\beta\le d\}\).

definitions.name: constant-gap Gaussian witness
definitions.construction: Let \(P^\dagger\) have \(X_t\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal X)\) and conditionally independent Gaussian arm outcomes with variance \(\sigma^2\). If \(\int_{\mathcal X}\{1-\pi_0(x)\}\,dx\ge1/2\), set the arm-zero and arm-one means to \(-\Delta_\dagger/2\) and \(\Delta_\dagger/2\), respectively; otherwise interchange those two means.

definitions.name: uniformly welfare-budgeted designs
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal Q)=\{\mathsf D: \mathsf D\ \text{is non-anticipating and }\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\mathcal R_T(P,\mathsf D)\le\rho\}\).

definitions.name: uniformly honest connected intervals
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak C_{T,\delta}(\mathsf D;\mathcal Q)=\{I_T:I_T\text{ is one }P\text{-independent Borel map }\mathcal Z_T\to\{[\ell,u]:(\ell,u)\in\mathbb R^2,\ \ell\le u\},\ \inf_{P\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb P_{P,\mathsf D}^{T}\{\theta(P)\in I_T(O_{1:T})\}\ge1-\delta\}\).

definitions.name: welfare-budgeted honest-width envelope
definitions.construction: \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal Q)=\inf_{\mathsf D\in\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal Q)}\inf_{I_T\in\mathfrak C_{T,\delta}(\mathsf D;\mathcal Q)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}|I_T(O_{1:T})|\), where the same \(P\)-independent Borel map \(I_T\) is used in every law, with value \(+\infty\) when \(\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal Q)=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: budgeted sequential targeting-gain modulus
definitions.construction: \(\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal Q)=\inf_{\mathsf D\in\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal Q)}\sup\{|\theta(P)-\theta(Q)|:P,Q\in\mathcal Q,\ \mathrm{KL}(\mathbb P_{P,\mathsf D}^{T}\Vert\mathbb P_{Q,\mathsf D}^{T})\le\kappa_\delta\}\) as an extended nonnegative real, with value \(+\infty\) when \(\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal Q)=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: finite resolution partition
definitions.construction: Fix a finite dyadic Borel partition \(\mathscr Q\) of \(\mathcal X\); its elements \(\mathsf Q\) are the resolution cells used only by the information-allocation relaxation.

definitions.name: active local target-separating alternatives
definitions.construction: For \(\mathsf Q\in\mathscr Q\) and \(w>0\), let \(\mathcal S_{\mathsf Q}(w)=\{s=(P,Q):P,Q\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}},\ P_X=Q_X,\ \mu_a^P=\mu_a^Q\ \text{on }\mathcal X\setminus\mathsf Q\ \text{for both }a,\ P_X\{x\in\mathsf Q:\tau_P(x)\tau_Q(x)<0\}>0,\ |\theta(P)-\theta(Q)|>2w\}\). Define \(\mathscr A(w)=\{\mathsf Q\in\mathscr Q:\mathcal S_{\mathsf Q}(w)\ne\varnothing\}\); exactly these cells are active.

definitions.name: one-sample local Gaussian information coefficients
definitions.construction: For \(s=(P,Q)\in\mathcal S_{\mathsf Q}(w)\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\), define \(k_{\mathsf Q,a}(s)=(2\sigma^2)^{-1}\mathbb E_{P_X}[\{\mu_a^P(X)-\mu_a^Q(X)\}^2\mid X\in\mathsf Q]\).

definitions.name: cellwise information-covering region
definitions.construction: For each active \(\mathsf Q\in\mathscr A(w)\), define \(\mathcal R_{\mathsf Q}(w)=\{(z_{\mathsf Q,0},z_{\mathsf Q,1})\in[0,\infty)^2:\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}z_{\mathsf Q,a}k_{\mathsf Q,a}(s)\ge\kappa_\delta\ \text{for every }s\in\mathcal S_{\mathsf Q}(w)\}\).

definitions.name: primal information-allocation relaxation
definitions.construction: Define \(\mathcal B(w)=\inf\{\sum_{\mathsf Q\in\mathscr A(w)}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}z_{\mathsf Q,a}:z_{\mathsf Q}\in\mathcal R_{\mathsf Q}(w)\ \text{for every }\mathsf Q\in\mathscr A(w)\}\), with the infimum in the extended nonnegative reals.

definitions.name: measure-valued semi-infinite-LP dual
definitions.construction: Define \(\mathcal D(w)=\sup\{\kappa_\delta\sum_{\mathsf Q\in\mathscr A(w)}\lambda_{\mathsf Q}(\mathcal S_{\mathsf Q}(w)):\lambda_{\mathsf Q}\ge0,\ \int_{\mathcal S_{\mathsf Q}(w)}k_{\mathsf Q,a}(s)\,d\lambda_{\mathsf Q}(s)\le1\ \text{for every }(\mathsf Q,a)\in\mathscr A(w)\times\mathcal A\}\).

definitions.name: implicit allocation width
definitions.construction: For \(n\in\mathbb N\), define \(w_n=\inf\{w>0:\mathcal B(w)\le n\}\) in the extended nonnegative reals.

definitions.name: allocation-guided exploration and interval handle
definitions.construction: Use the primal--dual programs \(\mathcal B(w)\) and \(\mathcal D(w)\) to select arm-specific cell quotas at the implicit level \(w_n\) with \(n=T\); realize those quotas through predictable dyadic exploration that prices each pull by an upper confidence bound for \(|\tau_P|\), and feed the realized local counts into polynomial approximation for the positive-part term plus a bias-aware augmented score for the benchmark term and one connected interval.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathsf D\) be one fixed non-anticipating design. First, if \(P,Q\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}\) induce the same observed trajectory law under \(\mathsf D\), and \(s_a^{P,\mathsf D}(x)>0\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\) and both \(a\in\mathcal A\), then \(\theta(P)=\theta(Q)\). Conversely, suppose there are \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(x_0\in\mathcal X\), \(r_0\in(0,1/2)\), and \(\eta>0\) such that the positive-uniform-mass set \(B=\{x:\|x-x_0\|_\infty<r_0\}\) is contained in \(\mathcal X\), \(\Delta_\dagger+\eta\le2M\), and \(\eta r_0^{-\beta}\le L\). Suppose \(\mathsf D\) assigns arm \(a\) with probability zero whenever the current context lies in \(B\), for every round and every observed history, and \(\mathbb E_{X\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal X)}[\psi_{x_0,r_0}(X)\{a\pi_0(X)+(1-a)(1-\pi_0(X))\}]>0\). Define \(P\) and \(Q\) to have uniform contexts and conditionally independent Gaussian innovations with the common scale \(\sigma\). Under both laws the mean of arm \(1-a\) is \(M\); the mean of arm \(a\) is \(M-\Delta_\dagger\) under \(P\) and \(M-\Delta_\dagger-\eta\psi_{x_0,r_0}(x)\) under \(Q\). Because the declared parameter domains give \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), the uniform density obeys the same envelope, so \(P,Q\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}\), \(\mathbb P_{P,\mathsf D}^{T}=\mathbb P_{Q,\mathsf D}^{T}\), and \(|\theta(P)-\theta(Q)|=\eta\mathbb E_{X\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal X)}[\psi_{x_0,r_0}(X)\{a\pi_0(X)+(1-a)(1-\pi_0(X))\}]>0\).
statements.justification: The two directions distinguish genuine observed-law identification from irreducible ambiguity created by an adaptive design that never reveals a benchmark-relevant arm on a positive-mass region.
statements.gap: LuedtkeVanDerLaan2016OptimalValue studies optimal value as an observed-data functional under a supplied observation law, while adaptive-policy inference papers impose positivity for fixed-policy scores; neither gives an observational-equivalence construction tied to history-dependent zero exposure and the benchmark-relative targeting gain.
statements.consumer: The result gives the frontier a sharp information boundary: attaining designs must create exposure wherever the benchmark makes the suppressed arm relevant, and no interval rule based only on the trajectory can repair a violated boundary.

statements.statement: Because the declared parameter domains give \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), the uniform context density of \(P^\dagger\) obeys the stated density envelope directly. The explicit law \(P^\dagger\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\Delta_0,b_0}^{\mathrm{fg}}\), and \(\mathcal P_{\Delta_0,b_0}^{\mathrm{fg}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}\). Hence both the fixed-gap and Hölder--margin classes are nonempty under the stated parameter domains.
statements.justification: An explicit common witness prevents the frontier from being driven by mutually inconsistent density, margin, gap, mean-bound, or benchmark-exposure constants.
statements.gap: Contextual-bandit rate theorems ordinarily suppress compatibility of fixed class constants; this result records the witness needed when the fixed-gap subclass is itself a theorem domain.
statements.consumer: The feasibility supporting lemma and fixed-gap frontier theorem optimize over genuine law classes rather than obtaining vacuous bounds over an empty parameter space.

statements.statement: The local margin condition implies the global envelope \(P_X\{0<|\tau_P(X)|\le u\}\le\overline C u^\alpha\) for every \(u>0\): use the local bound for \(u\le\delta_0\), and for \(u>\delta_0\) use probability at most one and \(1\le\delta_0^{-\alpha}u^\alpha\). By PerchetRigollet2013CovariateBandits, Theorem 5.1 and Proposition 3.1, there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the displayed class constants, such that \(cT^{r_{\beta,\alpha,d}}\le\rho_{\mathrm{feas}}(T;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\le CT^{r_{\beta,\alpha,d}}\). Passing from their bounded-reward experiment to the present fixed-scale Gaussian regression experiment is a routine tail-model translation. In particular, \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), and \(\alpha=1/5\) give \(r_{1,1/5,1}=3/5\), so \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{1,1/5}^{\mathrm{HM}})=+\infty\) whenever \(\rho<cT^{3/5}\).
statements.justification: This cited sanity reduction marks the empty-design regime before any honest-width branch is considered.
statements.gap: PerchetRigollet2013CovariateBandits, Theorem 5.1 gives the same Hölder--margin minimax regret exponent under its local margin formulation, and Proposition 3.1 gives the finite-margin restriction \(\alpha\beta\le d\); extending the local inequality by the probability bound and translating bounded rewards to fixed-scale Gaussian noise are routine and are not independent contributions.
statements.consumer: The supporting lemma retains the \(\rho=T^{3/5}\) early-kill threshold and prevents a width formula from being asserted in an infeasible regime.

statements.statement: For every law class \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}\), every \(\mathsf D\in\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal Q)\), every single \(P\)-independent Borel map \(I_T\in\mathfrak C_{T,\delta}(\mathsf D;\mathcal Q)\), and every \(P,Q\in\mathcal Q\) satisfying \(\mathrm{KL}(\mathbb P_{P,\mathsf D}^{T}\Vert\mathbb P_{Q,\mathsf D}^{T})\le\kappa_\delta\), \(\max\{\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}|I_T(O_{1:T})|,\mathbb E_{Q,\mathsf D}|I_T(O_{1:T})|\}\ge(1-2\delta)|\theta(P)-\theta(Q)|/2\). If \(P_X=Q_X\), then the adaptive Gaussian likelihood obeys the exact decomposition \(\mathrm{KL}(\mathbb P_{P,\mathsf D}^{T}\Vert\mathbb P_{Q,\mathsf D}^{T})=(2\sigma^2)^{-1}\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}\sum_{t=1}^T\{\mu_{A_t}^P(X_t)-\mu_{A_t}^Q(X_t)\}^2\). Consequently, \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal Q)\ge(1-2\delta)\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal Q)/2\) without restricting the design or the observed-trajectory interval map.
statements.justification: Coverage, rather than the risk of a nominated estimator, is converted into target separation under the exact adaptive information geometry.
statements.gap: KaufmannCappeGarivier2016Complexity controls adaptive decision events and CaiLow2004 controls expected confidence-interval length in fixed experiments; neither result includes a welfare-constrained contextual trajectory or the targeting-gain modulus.
statements.consumer: Every proposed branch of the width frontier must pass through this theorem, so an attaining interval cannot evade the lower bound by changing its center or shape.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(c,C,c_1,C_1>0\), depending only on \(\Delta_0,b_0,M,\sigma,\delta\) and the context-density constants, such that for \(C_1\log T\le\rho\le c_1T\), \(c\rho^{-1/2}\le W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\Delta_0,b_0}^{\mathrm{fg}})\le C\rho^{-1/2}\). The lower inequality holds for every non-anticipating design and every honest interval. The upper inequality is attained by an explicit explore-then-track design that learns the gap sign, spends the remaining budget on the inferior treatment, and reports one connected predictably weighted interval. Relative to SimchiLeviWang2023BanditExperimentalDesign, this is a strict strengthening from point-estimator error for a noncontextual treatment-effect gap to all honest intervals for the nonlinear contextual targeting gain with a \(P\)-independent benchmark.
statements.justification: This theorem isolates the compulsory \(\rho^{-1/2}\) obstruction and verifies that benchmark cancellation cannot remove it.
statements.gap: SimchiLeviWang2023BanditExperimentalDesign matches regret and treatment-effect estimation error for finite arms, while HadadEtAl2021AdaptiveConfidenceIntervals treats fixed-arm means under supplied adaptive propensities; neither gives an all-procedure honest-width statement for this causal gain.
statements.consumer: Trialists using a conventional benchmark obtain the exact price of protecting participants away from treatment ties and a design that pays no additional order penalty.

statements.statement: For every sufficiently small \(h\) and every integer \(m\le c h^{\alpha\beta-d}\), there are disjoint cells \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) and a finite Gaussian subexperiment contained in \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}}\) whose alternatives change only one arm on \(\bigcup_{j=1}^mB_j\), have Hölder amplitude of order \(h^\beta\), satisfy the margin condition, and separate \(\theta(P)\) by order \(m h^{d+\beta}\) without sign cancellation. For every non-anticipating \(\mathsf D\), the trajectory divergence between neighboring alternatives is bounded above by \(C h^{2\beta}\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}N_a^{\mathsf D}(\bigcup_{j=1}^mB_j)\).
statements.justification: The construction forces scalar targeting-gain separation, which ordinary label-flipping regret cubes can lose through cancellation.
statements.gap: PerchetRigollet2013CovariateBandits supplies localized regret alternatives and HanJiaoMukherjee2020LrNorms supplies scalar-functional mixtures; neither proves membership and adaptive information control for the same family.
statements.consumer: At \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), and \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\), this lemma is the early kill test for every proposed local-width exponent.

statements.statement: For a resolution partition \(\mathscr Q\), prove or disprove the information-saturation relation \(\mathcal B(w_n)\asymp n\) as \(n\to\infty\), where \(w_n=\inf\{w>0:\mathcal B(w)\le n\}\) and no power law is imposed. Establish weak duality \(\mathcal D(w)\le\mathcal B(w)\), determine whether equality of values holds under the stated Hölder--margin alternative sets without assuming dual attainment, and characterize any failure caused by discontinuities or inactive cells. Then determine whether, with \(n=T\), the handle \(\mathsf H_{T,\rho}\) can turn the resulting arm-specific cell quotas into one predictable design and one connected interval that uniformly satisfy participant-welfare loss at most \(\rho\), \(1-\delta\) honesty, and expected width of order \(w_n\) while respecting stochastic context-arrival capacities.
statements.justification: The semi-infinite covering program exposes the exact local information demand before asking whether random context arrivals and gap-priced exploration can realize it.
statements.gap: HuKallusMao2022SmoothContextualBandits controls regret under selective exploration, LiShiSimchiLevi2024PrivateAdaptiveDesign balances finite strata, and BibautEtAl2021PostContextualBanditInference stabilizes inference under supplied propensities; none proves primal saturation, dual value equality, and sequential quota realization for target-separating continuous-context alternatives under a hard welfare budget.
statements.consumer: A positive saturation and realization result supplies the implementable upper half of the frontier; a failure identifies whether alternative-set geometry, context capacity, or participant cost creates an additional width branch.

statements.statement: Determine, from the primitive Hölder-margin geometry, an explicit piecewise function of \((T,\rho,\beta,\alpha,d,\delta)\) and prove that both \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\) and \(\Omega_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\) are equivalent to it up to constants throughout \(\rho_{\mathrm{feas}}(T;\mathcal P_{\beta,\alpha}^{\mathrm{HM}})\le\rho\le T\). The derivation must locate every branch, budget-feasibility boundary, and flattening threshold, recover \(\rho^{-1/2}\) on \(\mathcal P_{\Delta_0,b_0}^{\mathrm{fg}}\), recover the fixed-design offline honest-width order when \(\rho\asymp T\), and resolve the \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\) Gaussian early-kill case.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: the rate and every transition are outputs rather than assumptions, so incorrect presolve exponents can be falsified.
statements.gap: No located paper combines an all-design honest-length converse, nonsmooth scalar optimal-value geometry, and a welfare-budget-saturating contextual allocation. SimchiLeviWang2023BanditExperimentalDesign and LiShiSimchiLevi2024PrivateAdaptiveDesign use estimation error in finite-arm or finite-feature models; PraharajKhamaru2025AvoidingPriceAdaptivity combines linear-functional asymptotic Wald inference with near-minimax regret but has neither uniform nonregular honesty nor a hard welfare budget; LuedtkeVanDerLaan2016OptimalValue and PonomarevSemenova2024LowerConfidenceBand do not optimize adaptive welfare-constrained data collection.
statements.consumer: The completed frontier tells experimenters the shortest credible post-trial statement about personalization gain compatible with a stated loss of participant welfare.

sampling_model.design: One \(P\)-independent non-anticipating contextual design chooses the known propensity \(e_t^{\mathsf D}(H_{t-1},X_t)\) from observed history and the fresh context; one \(P\)-independent Borel interval map is evaluated on the resulting observed trajectory.
sampling_model.units: The contexts are independent draws from a stationary density on \([0,1]^d\); the observed reward satisfies \(Y_t=\mu_{A_t}(X_t)+\sigma\varepsilon_t\) with fresh conditionally independent standard-normal innovations.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment satisfies \(A_t\mid(H_{t-1},X_t)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e_t^{\mathsf D})\), and only the selected-arm reward \(Y_t\) is observed.
sampling_model.overlap: No exogenous propensity floor is imposed; the design must generate any exploration needed for honesty while satisfying \(\sup_P\mathcal R_T(P,\mathsf D)\le\rho\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The attaining handle uses predictable local regression, polynomial approximation for the positive-part functional, and a bias-aware augmented score; all nuisance accuracy must be derived from the design-generated local counts.

estimand_functional: \(\theta(P)=\mathbb E_{P_X}[\tau_P(X)_+-\pi_0(X)\tau_P(X)]\), with frontier \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal Q)=\inf_{\mathsf D\in\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal Q)}\inf_{I_T\in\mathfrak C_{T,\delta}(\mathsf D;\mathcal Q)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}|I_T(O_{1:T})|\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1, 2, 5, and 6 give and attain a Pareto product frontier between participant regret and treatment-effect point-estimation error in a finite-armed experiment.
Theorem 5.1 gives the minimax regret exponent under the local Hölder--margin condition, and Proposition 3.1 yields \(\alpha\beta\le d\) for finite \(\alpha\).
The local asymptotic minimax result bounds regular ATE estimation under every covariate- and history-dependent assignment design.
Theorem 1 characterizes pathwise differentiability of the optimal value and Theorem 2 gives online one-step inference under a negligible rule-value remainder.
The paper derives minimax rates for nonsmooth \(L_r\)-functionals by polynomial approximation and moment-matching priors in fixed Gaussian white noise.
The lower and upper results match a CATE mean-squared-error versus regret frontier for finitely many contexts with fixed-order gaps.
The central theorem gives a studentized central limit theorem for predictably weighted augmented inverse-propensity estimators of fixed arm values.
The CADR theorem obtains asymptotic normality for a fixed contextual-policy value by conditional-variance stabilization.
Theorem 1 constructs nonasymptotic doubly robust confidence sequences for a fixed off-policy value under predictable logging policies.

The paper constructs one-sided lower confidence bands for optimal welfare that remain valid regardless of the margin condition; uniform separation and margin behavior govern its first-order welfare--precision comparison.
The main theorem derives asymptotic normality and adaptive semiparametric efficiency for regular scalar targets under directional stability and verifies the condition for LinUCB.

Section 4.1, Theorem 1 proves stability and asymptotic normality for ordinary least squares under regularized EXP4, yielding asymptotically exact Wald intervals for fixed linear functionals; Section 4.2, Theorem 2 gives the same algorithm a near-minimax regret bound.

tldr: An adaptive experiment that protects current participants suppresses observations from inferior treatments, while a credible post-experiment claim about the gain from individualized targeting needs precisely those observations and becomes nonregular near treatment ties. A two-direction theorem identifies the gain from the observed trajectory law under positive arm exposure and constructs observationally equivalent Gaussian laws with separated gains when a benchmark-relevant arm has zero exposure. The project restricts inference to one common \(P\)-independent Borel trajectory-to-interval map, uses a local Tsybakov margin condition, verifies nonempty Hölder--margin and fixed-gap classes, converts coverage into an extended-valued scalar-functional modulus, and exposes the attaining bottleneck through a cellwise semi-infinite information-allocation primal and dual. The fixed-gap edge is \(\rho^{-1/2}\), while the complete Hölder-margin frontier requires proving or disproving implicit allocation saturation and realizing its quotas under the welfare budget. The published Perchet--Rigollet feasibility exponent supplies a cited sanity boundary; \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), and \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\) serve as the mandatory early kill test.

project_justification.gap: Existing regret--inference Pareto results concern point-estimation error for finite-arm treatment gaps or finitely many fixed-gap strata. Praharaj and Khamaru obtain asymptotic Wald inference for fixed linear functionals and near-minimax regret from one linear contextual-bandit design, but not uniform nonregular honest width under a hard welfare budget. Other adaptive confidence-interval results take the logging design as given and target fixed policy values. Optimal-value inference treats the tie nonregularity but does not price exploration by participant welfare. None of these results characterizes the honest expected-width envelope over both designs and common observed-trajectory interval maps.
project_justification.niche: The targeting gain \(\mathbb E[\tau_+-\pi_0\tau]\) joins a regular benchmark-evaluation component to a nonsmooth positive-part component. A welfare budget endogenizes the information geometry because sampling the locally inferior arm has gap-dependent cost. This creates a sequential ordered-modulus problem that is absent from both ordinary contextual regret and fixed-design functional estimation.
project_justification.fill: Positive cumulative exposure identifies the target from the observed trajectory law, whereas an explicit zero-exposure pair proves nonidentification on benchmark-relevant regions. Every reported interval is one common \(P\)-independent Borel map of the observed trajectory, and an explicit constant-gap Gaussian law verifies that both frontier domains are nonempty under mutually compatible primitive constants. The procedure-free coverage reduction makes the extended-valued sequential targeting-gain modulus the lower-bound object. Target-separating local alternative sets generate armwise conditional-Gaussian KL coefficients, a semi-infinite covering program, and a measure-valued dual; the open saturation question asks whether their implicit width level can be realized by welfare-priced predictable exploration and a bias-aware connected interval. The fixed-gap theorem anchors the compulsory branch, and the open kernel requires a matching rate with every threshold derived from primitives.

related_work: Simchi-Levi and Wang establish a finite-arm Pareto frontier between regret and treatment-effect point-estimation error; Theorem 5 is written as the strict honest-width strengthening relevant here. Perchet and Rigollet, Theorem 5.1 and Proposition 3.1, supply the Hölder--margin minimax regret exponent and the restriction \(\alpha\beta\le d\); the supporting feasibility lemma first extends their local margin inequality by the probability bound and then uses a routine fixed-scale Gaussian translation rather than claiming an independent contribution. Hu, Kallus, and Mao supply the selective local-regression architecture. Luedtke and van der Laan locate the pathwise differentiability boundary of optimal value. Han, Jiao, and Mukherjee are cited only for nonsmooth fixed-Gaussian polynomial-approximation and moment-matching methodology, not for the adaptive regression experiment used here. Kaufmann, Cappé, and Garivier provide the allocation-agnostic sequential change of measure and the standard conditional Gaussian innovation framework, while Cai and Low provide the coverage-to-length modulus logic. Hadad and coauthors, Bibaut and coauthors, Waudby-Smith and coauthors, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas, and Shen and coauthors provide adaptive score, martingale, anytime-valid, efficiency, and stability tools for regular or fixed-policy targets; they inform the upper construction but do not determine this envelope. Praharaj and Khamaru, Section 4.1, Theorem 1 and Section 4.2, Theorem 2, construct one regularized EXP4 design with asymptotically exact Wald inference for fixed linear functionals and near-minimax regret; this is informed-by prior art because pointwise linear-functional asymptotics and an unconstrained regret guarantee do not deliver uniform honest minimax width for a nonregular positive-part target under a hard welfare budget. Li, Shi, and Simchi-Levi balance regret and CATE error over finitely many contexts, whereas the present bottleneck is learning and pricing continuous small-gap regions. Ponomarev and Semenova construct one-sided lower confidence bands for optimal welfare that remain valid regardless of the margin condition; uniform separation and margin behavior separately govern their first-order welfare--precision comparison, while two-sided budgeted adaptive width remains outside their result.
technical_internal_limitation: The exponent suggested by a regret packing is not automatically an exponent for the scalar targeting gain. Balanced sign flips can cancel in \(\mathbb E[\tau_+-\pi_0\tau]\), and a local design can concentrate information on precisely the cells a naive packing treats symmetrically. No local branch is part of the contribution until the alternatives in Lemma 6 are shown to belong to the class, separate the scalar target, and obey the adaptive likelihood inequality at the proposed budget.
honest_scope: Two-direction exposure identification, common class nonemptiness, coverage reduction for common observed-trajectory interval maps, the fixed-gap frontier, and the target-separating bump lemma are theorem obligations, not presumed facts. The feasibility exponent is a cited sanity reduction from PerchetRigollet2013CovariateBandits, Theorem 5.1 and Proposition 3.1, after the local margin bound is extended globally with \(\overline C=\max\{C_0,\delta_0^{-\alpha}\}\) and bounded rewards are translated routinely to fixed-scale Gaussian noise. The zero-exposure construction is a localized Gaussian identification diagnostic inside the Hölder--margin class, and its geometric and design conditions are local to that theorem rather than frontier assumptions. The sequential modulus and width envelope both equal \(+\infty\) when the uniformly feasible design class is empty. The exact Hölder-local rate, the number and locations of budget branches, strong duality or attainment for the semi-infinite allocation program, information saturation \(\mathcal B(w_n)\asymp n\), and sequential realization of its quotas are answer-open. At \(\rho\asymp T\), the result must reduce to fixed-design honest inference for the positive-part functional; on the fixed-gap subclass it must reduce to \(\rho^{-1/2}\); below \(T^{r_{\beta,\alpha,d}}\), the design class is empty. Smoothness adaptation, unknown variance, more than two treatments, and anytime-valid coverage are outside the claimed frontier.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Procedure-free fixed-gap converse joined to the unresolved Hölder-local width frontier.
seed_details.summary: Characterize the minimax expected length over every adaptive design and honest interval, derive all welfare-budget branches, and attain them with one design and interval.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction formulates participant regret against treatment-effect precision; Theorems 1, 2, 5, and 6 and their proofs derive and attain a product frontier through suboptimal-arm counts; the Conclusion leaves richer action models open, and the shrinking-gap discussion leaves an intermediate regime unmatched.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace estimator-risk separation by two-law simultaneous-coverage separation, then replace a global suboptimal-arm count by a context-local count whose price is the unknown treatment gap.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for honest expected width, optimal-value gain, contextual bandits, and welfare or regret budgets found fixed-policy intervals and regular efficiency results but no all-design width envelope.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Simchi-Levi and Wang because confidence width is just estimation error.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their objective fixes a point estimator and a finite-arm linear gap; uniform interval coverage for \(\tau_+\) requires target-separating local alternatives and remains meaningful when pointwise asymptotic variance does not.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Scalar-functional local modulus under endogenous arm-specific information.
seed_details.summary: Build sign-asymmetric Hölder-margin Gaussian mixtures that separate the targeting gain and characterize their adaptive ordered modulus.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction distinguishes optimal-rule learning from optimal-value inference; Theorem 1 proves pathwise differentiability exactly away from noisy ties, Theorem 2 controls an online one-step estimator through rule-value remainder conditions, and the Discussion records the asymmetry between lower and two-sided inference.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the assumed negligible value remainder by an explicit coverage-testing modulus and construct alternatives whose scalar positive-part integrals cannot cancel.
seed_details.destination_search: Han, Jiao, and Mukherjee provide polynomial and fuzzy-prior machinery for nonsmooth scalar functionals, while Perchet and Rigollet provide Hölder-margin bumps; no source combines either with adaptive arm-specific likelihood.
seed_details.red_team: The margin condition makes the optimal value regular, so Luedtke and van der Laan already imply the rate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem is pointwise and requires a remainder rate; union honesty along shrinking ties and endogenous exploration is exactly where that remainder is first order.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Uniform budget-saturating exploration and a connected attaining interval.
seed_details.summary: Learn continuous cheap-to-explore regions, saturate the welfare budget, and derive a uniform martingale limit with an explicit optimization-bias envelope.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction turns privacy-motivated participant welfare into an error--regret design problem; the ConSE theorem and proof learn finite context frequencies and balance second-stage trial lengths, while the lower proof uses Rademacher alternatives and adaptive KL; the concluding discussion retains finite contexts and fixed-order gaps.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace finite-stratum arrival counts by predictable local-polynomial confidence cells and prove a simultaneous lower bound on cellwise information and upper bound on gap-weighted welfare expenditure.
seed_details.destination_search: Hu, Kallus, and Mao supply selective smooth exploration, while Bibaut and coauthors supply variance stabilization; no located theorem derives both under a prescribed welfare budget.
seed_details.red_team: ConSE with a fine partition immediately handles continuous contexts.
seed_details.rebuttal: A fixed partition neither learns vanishing-gap geometry nor controls approximation bias, and its welfare price can be dominated by cells whose gap is estimated too late.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Efficiency bound for the regular fixed-gap edge under a welfare budget.
seed_details.summary: Derive the target-direction efficiency bound after optimizing predictable exploration under a fixed-gap welfare constraint and construct an attaining one-step interval.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction allows assignments based on covariates and past outcomes; the LAN theorem derives an all-design least-favorable information bound and the attaining section uses pilot-based Neyman allocation; the paper does not impose a welfare cost or shrinking positivity.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Add the gap-priced allocation constraint to the least-favorable information optimization before taking the LAN limit, instead of optimizing variance over unconstrained propensities.
seed_details.destination_search: Shen and coauthors now characterize directional-stability efficiency for regular scalar targets, which occupies much of the unconstrained stability lane but not the welfare-constrained design optimization.
seed_details.red_team: Armstrong's all-design efficiency theorem already permits adaptive assignments and therefore includes the budgeted subclass.
seed_details.rebuttal: Restriction to a budgeted subclass changes the attainable information set and its optimizer; nevertheless this seed is narrower than the full honest-width frontier and was not selected.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Choose a terminal policy while controlling participant welfare during learning.
seed_details.summary: Optimize terminal policy regret under a hard cumulative participant-welfare budget and derive an oracle inequality over Hölder-margin laws.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction poses contextual treatment choice; the ABSE theorem and proof balance bin refinement with successive elimination and the lower-bound discussion identifies the sharp Hölder-margin exponent; the conclusion emphasizes regret rather than uncertainty about the scalar gain.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Separate in-experiment welfare expenditure from terminal policy regret instead of using cumulative regret as the sole objective.
seed_details.destination_search: Adaptive policy-learning papers condition on diminishing exploration, and budgeted bandit papers optimize reward or resource constraints; the exact terminal-versus-participant frontier remains plausible but does not answer the stated interval question.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine constrained-regret restatement of contextual bandit theory.
seed_details.rebuttal: The two losses occur at different horizons and can yield a nontrivial allocation frontier, but the consumer is less direct than honest inference, so the seed was not selected.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: When do unweighted and variance-stabilized adaptive intervals agree under budgeted exploration?
seed_details.summary: Derive the observable target-direction information threshold at which an ordinary one-step interval and a stabilized adaptive interval share a limit law, and the shrinking-exploration side where they diverge.
seed_details.anchor_read: Armstrong's LAN construction identifies the optimal regular information bound, while the achieving designs rely on stable pilot estimates; its conclusion does not characterize failure under random, anisotropic information growth.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain the random predictable quadratic variation under welfare-driven shrinking propensities instead of replacing it by a deterministic positive-overlap limit.
seed_details.destination_search: Shen and coauthors establish directional stability in 2026 and verify LinUCB, making a generic stability frontier occupied; a novelty claim would need the nonsmooth targeting-gain direction and a budget-derived threshold.
seed_details.red_team: Directional stability already gives the exact equivalence condition.
seed_details.rebuttal: It settles regular targets under an imposed stability property but does not derive stability from a welfare budget; still, the overlap with that preprint lowers this seed's novelty rank.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Procedure-free fixed-gap honest-width lower bound with benchmark noncancellation.
seed_details.summary: Show that every honest interval has expected width at least order \(\rho^{-1/2}\) when the fixed benchmark places positive mass on the inferior arm, and match it with an adaptive interval.
seed_details.anchor_read: The product lower bound changes one suboptimal arm and converts its expected count into KL, while EXP3E supplies the matching count; the proof targets treatment-effect estimation error rather than simultaneous coverage.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Perturb the inferior regression while preserving the optimal policy, compute the induced change in the benchmark-relative gain, and invoke two-law coverage rather than estimator deviation.
seed_details.destination_search: Hadad and coauthors explicitly leave optimal worst-case confidence width open; no fixed-gap contextual honest-width result was located.
seed_details.red_team: The result is only Simchi-Levi and Wang with an interval wrapped around their estimator.
seed_details.rebuttal: The lower bound quantifies over all interval centers and needs benchmark-sensitive target separation, while the upper bound must be uniformly honest after adaptive sign learning.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Anytime-valid inference for an adaptively learned optimal-value gain.
seed_details.summary: Construct a confidence sequence for the targeting gain that remains valid under stopping and derive its width under Hölder-margin alternatives.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction separates policy optimization from off-policy evaluation; Theorem 1 builds a doubly robust betting confidence sequence by Ville's inequality for a fixed policy value; the Conclusion leaves uniform inference over a policy family open.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed target-policy pseudo-outcome by a lower envelope over learned policies and account for the positive-part optimization bias before applying a test supermartingale.
seed_details.destination_search: Ponomarev and Semenova give one-sided offline optimal-welfare bands, but no anytime two-sided gain interval was found.
seed_details.red_team: Uniformly unioning the fixed-policy confidence sequences immediately covers the optimizer.
seed_details.rebuttal: An uncountable smooth policy class and vanishing propensities make the union nonsharp, and the selected optimum changes the target; however anytime validity adds logarithmic overhead outside the fixed-horizon question, so the seed was not selected.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Finite-sample randomization inversion for the targeting gain.
seed_details.summary: Invert an assignment-orbit test to obtain a finite-sample interval for personalization gain under adaptive assignment.
seed_details.anchor_read: The paper obtains finite-sample coverage from predictable betting supermartingales, not assignment symmetry; its design-based remark conditions on potential outcomes but still targets a time-varying treatment contrast.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Find a group action preserving an adaptively generated assignment law while imputing the missing optimized potential outcomes.
seed_details.destination_search: Randomization-inference and conformal searches did not locate a nontrivial symmetry orbit for response-adaptive propensities and the weak-null optimal-value gain.
seed_details.red_team: Adaptive assignments are not exchangeable, so the required permutation group does not exist without conditioning away nearly all information.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the stated design class; this seed is dropped rather than padded into the retained set.

literature_map.anchor: SimchiLeviWang2023BanditExperimentalDesign is the direct tradeoff anchor: its Introduction states the participant-welfare versus precision conflict, Theorem 1 gives the allocation-count lower product, Theorems 2 and 6 characterize Pareto optimality, Theorem 5 supplies the attaining concentration result, and the shrinking-gap discussion leaves an unmatched intermediate regime. The present kernel changes the inferential object from point error in a linear arm gap to the expected length of every honest interval for a nonsmooth contextual gain.
adjacent_threads: KaufmannCappeGarivier2016Complexity and CaiLow2004 provide the two ingredients for a procedure-free converse: adaptive likelihood decomposition and coverage-to-expected-length modulus. Neither prices information by a contextual welfare loss.

PerchetRigollet2013CovariateBandits, Theorem 5.1 and Proposition 3.1, establish the Hölder--margin minimax regret exponent under a local margin condition and the finite-margin restriction \(\alpha\beta\le d\); the global envelope follows from probability at most one, and the fixed-scale Gaussian feasibility step is a routine translation. HuKallusMao2022SmoothContextualBandits establishes selective exploration. Their hard instances separate cumulative policy mistakes, which need not separate the scalar targeting gain.

LuedtkeVanDerLaan2016OptimalValue locates the tie nonregularity, while PonomarevSemenova2024LowerConfidenceBand constructs one-sided lower confidence bands that remain valid regardless of the margin condition and uses uniform separation and margin behavior to characterize the first-order welfare--precision comparison. Neither paper optimizes a data-collection design under a participant budget.

HanJiaoMukherjee2020LrNorms supplies polynomial approximation and moment-matching priors for the positive-part component under fixed Gaussian information. The destination problem replaces that information by adaptive local arm counts.

HadadEtAl2021AdaptiveConfidenceIntervals, BibautEtAl2021PostContextualBanditInference, WaudbySmithEtAl2024AnytimeOffPolicy, and CookMishlerRamdas2024EfficientAdaptiveInference provide predictable weighting, variance stabilization, confidence sequences, and efficient regular ATE estimation. Their policy or target is fixed and their exploration is supplied rather than selected under \(\rho\).

Armstrong2022ExperimentalDesignEfficiency and ShenEtAl2026DirectionalStability give all-design regular efficiency and target-direction stability, respectively. The targeting gain is nonregular near ties, and neither paper derives the feasible information set from participant welfare.

PraharajKhamaru2025AvoidingPriceAdaptivity, Section 4.1, Theorem 1 and Section 4.2, Theorem 2, pairs asymptotically valid Wald inference for fixed linear functionals with near-minimax regret for regularized EXP4. It does not minimize uniform honest width for a nonregular positive-part functional or impose a hard participant-welfare budget.

LiShiSimchiLevi2024PrivateAdaptiveDesign learns finite context frequencies and matches a CATE-error versus regret product under fixed-order gaps. Continuous cells, vanishing gaps, scalar functional cancellation, and uniform interval coverage remain absent.
literature_map.subsumption_check: No located paper defines or solves the infimum over welfare-feasible adaptive designs and common \(P\)-independent uniformly honest interval maps for \(\mathbb E[\tau_+-\pi_0\tau]\). PraharajKhamaru2025AvoidingPriceAdaptivity and ShenEtAl2026DirectionalStability require regular linear or pathwise-differentiable scalar targets and obtain pointwise asymptotic Wald inference; neither treats union honesty at ties nor chooses the information process under a hard welfare constraint. Fixed-policy confidence sequences and one-sided optimal-welfare bands likewise do not subsume the kernel.

novelty_justification.precise_gap: The first result characterizes regret against point-estimation error for a finite-arm linear treatment gap. The second characterizes pointwise regularity and online inference for optimal value under a supplied design and a negligible rule-value remainder. PraharajKhamaru2025AvoidingPriceAdaptivity shows that one stable linear contextual-bandit algorithm can retain near-minimax regret and support asymptotic Wald inference for fixed linear functionals, but it does not address a nonsmooth targeting gain, uniform honest expected width, or a hard welfare budget. None of these results derives the Hölder-margin transition map for the scalar targeting gain.
novelty_justification.why_not_subsumed: Adaptive change of measure alone does not ensure that alternatives separate \(\theta(P)\), and an optimal-value influence function alone does not control the tie remainder uniformly. The proposed modulus couples both issues and retains the design as an optimization variable. The benchmark inferior-mass condition prevents the fixed-gap perturbation from disappearing through benchmark cancellation.
novelty_justification.chosen_kernel_reason: The complete frontier takes the published feasibility boundary as a supporting sanity reduction and makes the new welfare-budget-to-honest-width implications, the regular \(\rho^{-1/2}\) obstruction, the target-separating adaptive construction, the nonsmooth local modulus, and the attaining exploration rule parts of one theorem program. It also contains a decisive falsification point: any proposed formula must work at \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), and \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\).
novelty_justification.adversarial_boundary: A packed sign-symmetric contextual-bandit construction can have large classification regret separation but zero targeting-gain separation. Lemma 6 therefore demands a sign-asymmetric scalar-separated family and exact adaptive KL accounting before the local rate is credited.
